details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:231-237, 290-296 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A.3's `fallback_notify` action omits the `fb` suffix rename that A.4 requires to mark the fallback as sent.
  WHY: Without the rename, subsequent ticks can re-emit fallback notifications for the same terminal PR until the marker is stale-swept.
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:251-259, 347-353 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A.6 does not specify what a subscriber should do when its dead-man's-switch Routine fires after the master dies and the PR is terminal.
  WHY: The subscriber may take no terminal-report or notification action, leaving the original pushing session without the PR's terminal verdict.
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:131, 175-185; 196, 213-237 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The plan does not prevent overlapping hourly master ticks when a tick takes longer than an hour.
  WHY: Concurrent ticks can both act as keeper and race on subscriber renewals and hand-back Routine name updates; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this MAJOR.
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:64, 95, 169-173 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The title-renaming condition depends on comparing counts with prior title values, but the plan does not specify how a stateless master retrieves those values after compaction.
  WHY: After compaction the comparison may cause stale titles or repeated renames, diverging from the documented stateless behavior.
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:200-205, 211 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A.4 specifies no tie-breaker for fixer Routines with equal `created_at` timestamps.
  WHY: Fixer selection can be nondeterministic and divert a due-fix hand-back from the intended session; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this NIT or MAJOR.
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:235-243 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A.5 does not specify recovery for partial failure while creating the master session, tick Routine, and first-tick trigger.
  WHY: A failed creation call can leave the master without scheduled wakeups or leave partial state without a specified retry or cleanup path; severity disagreement: one reviewer rated this NIT.
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:395-403 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: P5 specifies no recovery path when its 30-day preflight retry window expires while the preflight is still failing.
  WHY: The project can remain blocked after legacy per-PR checker creation has been removed, without a specified recovery path.
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:153-162, 200-211 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The master identifies owned Routines using prompt-text tokens without verifying their authority or relationship to the master's scope.
  WHY: An unrelated Routine containing matching tokens could be treated as a subscriber and have its state consumed or renamed; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this NIT or MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The plan claims the dead-man's switch logic is tested, but the implementation steps (P1 step 5) do not enumerate tests for the switch cascade.
  expected_change_site: docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md Implementation Steps P1 step 5
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: P1 step 5 test list covers individual failure scenarios but lacks a test case ensuring the cascading failure of the dead-man switch (A.4 step 4) when subscriber wakeups also fail due to a sustained GitHub API outage.
- requirement: §6 naming immutability — "Every existing name is kept" and A.1 master tick Routine name must fit the consumer repo limit (≤60 chars).
  expected_change_site: docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md A.1 / Implementation Steps P1 / Phase P4 rollout
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: Plan fails to cross-check `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json` for Routine name lengths; implementation steps do not require computing `len("PR status master: " + owner_repo)` for every consumer and rejecting names over 60 characters. z-ai_glm-5_2 reports verifying all consumers are within the limit and says this is not a gap.
- requirement: Q6 "The decisions come from a new script, `.claude/scripts/check_in_master.py`; the model only executes its action list" together with A.4 step 4 "Read failure (exit-2 equivalent) → no renew, so the dead-man's switch (A.6) fires within 90 min."
  expected_change_site: docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md A.4 step 4 / Implementation Steps P1 step 5 (test list) / A.6 subscriber dead-man branch
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: P1 step 5 includes read failure → no renew but does not bound the simultaneous subscriber cascade, specify jitter or throttling, or cap N subscriber ensure and PR-read attempts during a sustained GitHub outage.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md: A.3 step 3 lines 231-232 vs A.4 step 4 lines 295-296
  PROBLEM: A.4 step 4 specifies that the terminal sent marker must be renamed to add an `fb` suffix to deduplicate fallback_notify across ticks ("A PR only counts as having had its fallback once: the marker's name is changed to `… sent <state> <sha7> fb` in the same action"), but A.3 step 3 lists only `PushNotification` and a reply line as the action for `fallback_notify` with no rename step.
  WHY: The master model following A.3 literally will send the PushNotification but never rename the Routine, so on every subsequent tick the script re-emits `fallback_notify` for the same terminal PR until the marker ages past 6h and is stale-swept.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md: A.6 lines 347-353
  PROBLEM: When the master dies and a subscriber's dead-man's switch fires, A.6 says the woken subscriber runs `check_in_status.py --hand-back` and if the PR is still open it recreates the hand-back and ensures the master. It does not specify what happens when the PR is terminal (merged/closed).
  WHY: If the master dies after pulling a subscriber forward for a terminal PR but before the subscriber's Routine fires, the subscriber wakes, finds a terminal PR, and takes no action — the terminal report and PushNotification are lost, and the original pushing session never learns the PR's outcome.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md: A.1 line 196, A.3 lines 213-237
  PROBLEM: The master tick Routine uses `cron_expression: 0 * * * *` (hourly) with no concurrency guard.
  WHY: A tick that takes longer than an hour results in two concurrent master invocations running the same action list against the same Routines.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md: A.4 step 2 lines 264-265
  PROBLEM: Fixer selection uses "newest `created_at` among `Role: fixer` Routines" with no tie-breaker for equal timestamps, while keeper election (A.4 step 1) explicitly specifies "ties broken by `id`."
  WHY: On extremely unlikely `created_at` collisions, the fixer selection is non-deterministic between equally-timed Routines, and a master-created fixer Routine could win over the original pushing session's Routine, diverting the due-fix hand-back.
  severity=NIT | confidence=2
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md: P5 Independence paragraph lines 395-403
  PROBLEM: The P5 stage re-checks its preflight daily via a one-shot self Routine for at most 30 days, and after that "stops at BLOCKED" with no specified recovery path.
  WHY: If the P5 preflight conditions are not met after 30 days (e.g., a legacy hand-back Routine persists), the chain terminates in BLOCKED state indefinitely, with no specified operator action, auto-retry, or fallback mechanism.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: NONE
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:64, 169-173
  PROBLEM: The statelessness guarantee conflicts with the A.3 instruction to rename the master session.
  WHY: If the master is stateless, it cannot retrieve the existing title to rename it after compaction, which could lead to redundant renaming attempts on every tick or stale titles, diverging from the documented intent.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:251-259
  PROBLEM: A.6 does not specify the subscriber recovery path when a PR is terminal after the master has died.
  WHY: The subscriber is woken but does not know how to handle a terminal PR in the master's absence; the original pushing session may receive no final report or PushNotification.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:200-205, 211
  PROBLEM: A.4 tie-breaker is missing when multiple fixer Routines have the same created_at timestamp.
  WHY: Multiple automated fixer routines can realistically share a created_at timestamp; an arbitrary choice may divert hand-back notifications from the actual fixer to a notified subscriber.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:131, 175-185
  PROBLEM: The plan does not specify how to handle cases where a tick takes longer than an hour.
  WHY: Overlapping tick invocations could run simultaneously, leading to race conditions in subscriber renewals and out-of-order hand-back Routine name updates.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:231-237, 290-296
  PROBLEM: Conflict between A.3 procedure (A.4) and A.4 rules regarding the `fb` suffix rename for fallback_notify.
  WHY: The procedure fails to rename the Routine with the fb suffix, so subsequent ticks will repeatedly re-emit fallback_notify for the same terminal PR until the marker is stale-swept.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:235-243
  PROBLEM: No recovery path specified for transient failures in creating the master session, tick Routine, or one-shot first-tick trigger.
  WHY: If creation fails transiently, the master may remain uninitialized or without scheduled wakeups until a manual retry or another pickup cycle, leaving the PR status system in a stalled state.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:399-403
  PROBLEM: No recovery path for P5 preflight remaining failing after its 30-day self-Routine expires.
  WHY: The system is left in a state where legacy checkers are removed but the stateless master is not operational, blocking all PR status updates permanently for the re
